name: Template — multi-step wizard
purpose: The page that walks a person through one task in ordered steps and ends with a receipt: progress indicator, one step visible at a time, a gated Next, a review step, and a confirmation. It contributes PAGE SCALE, real form steps, a review step and an end state - the step MECHANISM itself is Stepper's and is borrowed whole.
$provenance-note: NEW at #210 (wave 5, lane C) against the Layer-2 P2 fan-out brief - itinerary row 109. PROPOSED, NOT RULED. No registration was performed: no CATEGORIES entry, no MIGRATED_SNIPPETS entry, no component-types.json membership, no canon.css block, no _rulings.json line, no git operation. Deleting this pair costs nothing because nothing points at it.
$existence-question: READ THIS BEFORE KEEPING THE FILE. Stepper.reference.html is ALREADY an interactive wizard: step panels, validation-gated Next, back-navigation on completed dots, focus management, sr-live announcer. Row 109 is a missing PAGE, not a missing mechanism. What this template adds over Stepper is exactly four things: page scale (app bar + page head + frame); REAL form steps (Stepper's panels are demo prose that says so on its own face); a REVIEW step (Summary's dl with per-row Change links that jump back to the owning step - Stepper has none); and an END STATE (the Confirmation organism - Stepper's last Next writes a string to a live region and stops). ⬛ LIVE OUTCOME: if Dave rules that a wizard template is just Stepper with content poured in, DELETE this pair and mark row 109 Duplicate against component:stepper. That call is his.
$layer-note: The brief PROPOSED the meta key `layer`. meta.schema.json is additionalProperties:false with patternProperties '^\\$' only, so a bare `layer` key FAILS probe P-1 (probe_meta_schema.py). `$layer` is the legal form and is what is used here. A CORRECTION to the brief's proposed artefact-class convention, reported.

props.name: steps
props.$note: Drives the dots, the collapsed 'Step N of M' head, the track fill, the panels and the announcer from ONE source. The specimen carries four.

props.name: current
props.$note: 1-based. Advancing is gated by the current step's rules; going BACK never is.

props.name: reviewStep
props.$note: Renders Summary's dl with a Change control per row. Each Change carries the step index that owns the value.

props.name: endState
props.$note: When 'confirmation', the wizard's own action bar RETIRES on the last step and Confirmation's own actions take over - two competing action bars would otherwise stack.

variants.name: dots
variants.use: Container wider than 640px: the labelled dots stepper, with completed dots as real back-navigation buttons.

variants.name: collapsed
variants.use: Container 640px or narrower: Progress-tracker's 1784-86051 form - 'Step N of M' plus a continuous 4px track.

$composes: Stepper (step visuals + flow shape, class names KEPT), Progress-tracker (the visuals Stepper itself consumed - change them THERE), Form-layout (field groups + error summary), Summary (the review dl), Confirmation (the end state, including its entrance sequence and reduced-motion suppression), Headers (app bar), Button (press-physics partial).

accessibility.roles: role=progressbar on the collapsed track with aria-valuemin/max/now/text; each step panel is a <section> with an aria-label naming its number and title; the confirmation is role=group + aria-labelledby.
accessibility.keyboard: Back and Next are real buttons. Completed dots become real <button>s with an accessible name that says which step they return to and that it is completed. Every review row's Change is a real button. Nothing is reachable only by pointer.
accessibility.announcements: A persistent visually-hidden aria-live region announces 'Step N of M: <name>' on every move, so the change is heard whichever form (dots or track) is rendered. Focus moves to the new step's heading.
accessibility.states: aria-current="step" on the current dot; aria-invalid set and cleared per field; Next is gated, not disabled, so the reason for not advancing is stated rather than silently withheld (3.3.1).
accessibility.targets: Back/Next are 44px. The review Change controls have a REAL 44px box, not an invisible expander - see the antiPattern.
accessibility.$colourIsNeverAlone: Progress is carried by the step LABELS and 'Step N of M', never by the green fill. That is Dave's own #176 ruling, inherited: 'the label and the symbol must carry the contrast not the decoration.'
accessibility.$declaredAbsence: step/complete on background/default (and its inverse) are NOT in contrastPairs. MEASURED 1.98:1 in Mono light. Inherited from the roundel system by Dave's #176 word, not a regression introduced here. The GATED legs - the tick on the fill, and the step label on the page - ARE listed.

antiPatterns: Re-drawing the step visuals. They belong to Progress-tracker; Stepper already consumes them and this template consumes Stepper's. Three copies now exist and that duplication is receipt-flagged, not endorsed.
Disabling Next instead of gating it. A disabled Next tells a person nothing about what is missing. Next stays enabled and states the error (3.3.1).
Letting the wizard's action bar and the Confirmation's actions both render on the last step. The wizard's bar retires; two stacked primaries is a decision the person did not ask for.

Using an invisible ::before hit expander on tightly-stacked rows. MEASURED at #210 on the review list: a 10.1px control with a 44px invisible expander on a 36.6px row pitch OVERLAPPED its neighbours by ~7px. Every gate passed - the a11y target check sees a 44px expander and cannot see that two of them intersect. Give the control a REAL 44px box and let the row pitch grow.
Making a review row's value a link. The Change control is the affordance; a linked value gives two targets for one action.
REVIEW Treating this template as evidence that Confirmation is settled. Confirmation is a CANDIDATE (its meta carries 'REVIEW: no Figma node yet'). Borrowing it does not promote it.
